crossRefs.note: They began to accuse him, saying, “We found this man perverting the nation, forbidding paying taxes to Caesar, and…
But they insisted, saying, “He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee even to this…
and said to them, “You brought this man to me as one that perverts the people, and behold, having examined him before…
Neither has Herod, for I sent you to him, and see, nothing worthy of death has been done by him.
As he said these things to them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to be terribly angry, and to draw many things out…
For we have found this man to be a plague, an instigator of insurrections among all the Jews throughout the world, and…

parallels.note: The chief priests accused him of many things.

translations.web: The chief priests and the scribes stood, vehemently accusing him.
translations.bsb: Meanwhile, the chief priests and scribes stood there, vehemently accusing Him.
translations.kjv: And the chief priests and scribes stood and vehemently accused him.
translations.asv: And the chief priests and the scribes stood, vehemently accusing him.
